study_identification.author_journal_year: Xiao et al., Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2025
study_identification.title: Deviations From Normative Functioning Underlying Emotional Episodic Memory Revealed Cross-Scale Neurodiverse Alterations Linked to Affective Symptoms in Distinct Psychiatric Disorders

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate cross-scale neural dysfunctions related to affective symptoms in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD), bipolar disorder (BD), and schizophrenia (SZ) using a normative modeling approach on functional MRI data from an emotional episodic memory task. The study also aimed to identify cellular signatures underlying these dysfunctions using imaging transcriptomic analysis.

dataset_name.answer: Peking University; Peking University Sixth Hospital

quality_checking_detail.answer: Head motion correction using a six-parameter (rigid body) linear transformation. Incorrect responses and residual movement parameters were modeled as regressors of no interest.

response_variable.answer: Functional activation ('aversive - neutral' contrast in the retrieval phase) in 82 brain regions (Desikan-Killiany atlas)

predictor_variables.answer: Reaction time (RT) in the encoding and retrieval phase; Accuracy (ACC) in the retrieval phase

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study assessed the influence of age and sex on the normative model and found no significant effects. However, it did not explicitly address other potential nuisance factors like site effects, despite using data from two different centers.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: The normative model established based on behavior performances, sex, and age also showed a high correlation with current models, which implied that sex and age had no signi /uniFB01 cant effect on our normative model (Figure S5).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study performed a 10-fold cross-validation on the training dataset (HCtrain) to assess the internal validity of the normative model.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The internal evaluation of model generalizability of normative functioning underlying emotional episodic memory was assessed using 10-fold cross-validation applied to HCtrain...

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study used an independent dataset of healthy controls (HCtest) for external validation of the normative model.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: As external validation, we positioned each participant in HCtest within the normative range and further calculated the subject-level distribution similarity between HCtrain and HCtest cohort...

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study did not report any validation of the normative model on a dataset from a different domain.

diseases_studied.answer: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD); Bipolar Disorder (BD); Schizophrenia (SZ)

clinical_groups_age.answer: MDD: mean 25.1, sd 5.0; BD: mean 27.0, sd 5.3; SZ: mean 25.2, sd 5.6

deviation_metric.answer: z-score (deviation from the normative reference). Extreme deviations were defined by thresholding the z-value at z > 2.6 or z < -2.6.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Multiple linear regression was used to predict affective symptoms from individual deviations of brain regions with significant extreme deviations. Pearson correlation and root-mean-square error (RMSE) were used to assess model performance. Virtual lesion method was used to determine the feature weight of the model.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study identified distinct patterns of cross-scale neural alterations linked to affective symptoms in MDD, BD, and SZ, with macroscale dysfunctions embedded in non-overlapping emotional networks and associated with specific cell-type signatures.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Patients with MDD showed supranormal deviations in a network related to emotion perception and generation (EN 3), which were associated with anxiety/somatization symptoms. Patients with BD exhibited infranormal deviations in networks for cognitive appraisal and emotional reactivity (EN 2 and EN 4), associated with total depression scores. Patients with SZ had infranormal deviations in a working memory and response inhibition network (EN 1), linked to anxiety/depression symptoms. These macroscale alterations were associated with microglia in MDD, astrocytes in BD, and excitatory neurons in SZ.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The clinical sample size was relatively small. Non-overlapping measures for affective symptoms were used across disorders. Most patients with BD were in the euthymic stage. The potential confounding effects of medication cannot be entirely ruled out. Gene expression data from the AHBA may not fully represent the variability in cortical gene expression. The analysis was limited to the left hemisphere.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The findings provide a basis for understanding the neuropathological patterns of affective symptoms in psychiatric disorders and guiding individualized treatment. The cross-scale neural alterations may provide enlightening evidence of unique dysfunctional neural characteristics.
